title: Energy Cost of Density Defects in Fermi Seas
exact_target: Find the least energy needed to make particle-density excesses or holes in an infinite Fermi sea, including sharp lower-bound constants.

sources.citation: ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, UnsolvedMath, record 30001819 (OWR-5160-001). Catalogue curation under CC BY 4.0; definitions and English exposition added locally.
Mathematical Methods in Quantum Chemistry (2011), Oberwolfach Reports, DOI 10.4171/owr/2011/32, pp. 1769--1843; official report source and mathematical context.
Official EMS Press PDF of the same Oberwolfach report; PDF pages 23--24, printed pages 1791--1792.

status_qualification: The official report already proves a positive-density lower bound in d>=2. The remaining optimal-cost or sharp-constant task is more specific than the catalogue's title-only dated assessment. Dimensions, spin normalization, finite-relative-energy domain, and density admissibility must be retained; a trace of two infinite energies is not a valid definition.
